```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

results <- file.path("..", "outputs", "results")
num <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
cnt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)

# Source lines of one or more stages of a script in R/. The code shown in this
# document is therefore always the code in the repository.
stage <- function(script, ...) {
  x  <- readLines(file.path("..", "R", script), encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE)
  h  <- grep("^# STAGE ", x)
  id <- sub("^# STAGE ([0-9a-z]+).*", "\\1", x[h])
  from <- h - 1                       # the "# ====" line above each header
  to   <- c(from[-1] - 1, length(x))
  k <- match(c(...), id); stopifnot(!anyNA(k))
  unlist(Map(function(a, b) x[a:b], from[k], to[k]))
}
pipeline <- "VAAT-FUNC-01_wetland_pipeline_OpenSource.R"

fac   <- read_csv(file.path(results, "VAAT-FUNC-01_factor_indicators.csv"))
idx   <- read_csv(file.path(results, "VAAT-FUNC-01_index_by_region_period.csv"))
plots <- read_csv(file.path(results, "VAAT-FUNC-01_plots.csv"))
ref   <- read_csv(file.path("..", "data", "OpenS_data", "wet_ref_openS.csv"))
plots$nin <- sub("-.*", "", plots$kartleggingsenhet_1m2)

main_period <- "cycle1_2019to2024"
nat <- fac |> filter(period == main_period, region == "Norway")
val <- function(f) {
  r <- nat[nat$factor == f, ]
  paste0(num(r$mean), " [95% CI: ", num(r$ci_low), "–", num(r$ci_high), "]")
}
idx_nat <- idx |> filter(period == main_period, region == "Norway")
fac_lv <- c("Light", "Moisture", "pH", "Nitrogen")
reg_lv <- c("Norway", "Northern", "Central", "Western", "Eastern", "Southern")
extremes <- function(f) {
  r <- fac |> filter(period == main_period, factor == f, region != "Norway") |> arrange(mean)
  k <- nrow(r)
  paste0("lowest in ", r$region[1], " (", num(r$mean[1]), ") and highest in ",
         r$region[k], " (", num(r$mean[k]), ")")
}
```

## 1. Summary

1. **Background and rationale**:
Plant species differ in the light, moisture, soil reaction (pH) and nitrogen conditions they grow in. When the conditions in a wetland change, for example through drainage, woody encroachment or nitrogen deposition, the species composition shifts with them. These indicators measure how far the vegetation has shifted from what is expected for the wetland type.

2. **Methods**:
We use plant cover data from the national area-representative monitoring programme ANO and species indicator values from Tyler et al. (2021).
    - For each plot, we calculate the cover-weighted mean (community-weighted mean, CWM) of the indicator values.
    - The CWM is scaled against a reference distribution for the plot's wetland type, bootstrapped from generalised species lists.
    - Light, moisture and pH are two-sided: deviations in both directions lower the value. Nitrogen is one-sided: only enrichment counts.
    - Regional and national values come from an ordered beta regression with ANO site as a random effect.

3. **Interpretation**:
A value of 1 means that the species composition matches the reference for the wetland type.
Values decreasing towards 0 reflect a shift away from it. 0.6 is the limit for good ecological condition.

4. **Results and development needs**:
For ANO's first cycle (2019–2024, the first survey of each point, n = `r cnt(nat$n[1])` plots) the national values are: light `r val("Light")`, moisture `r val("Moisture")`, pH `r val("pH")` and nitrogen `r val("Nitrogen")`. All are above 0.6.
The main development needs are regionalised species lists, references for the wetland types that lack them, and validation against independent data.

## 2. About the underlying data {#sec-about}

Three types of data are used:

- plant community data from ANO (observations);
- generalised species lists from Nature in Norway, NiN (reference): dataset B12 "Planter og lav på myr" from Artsdatabanken;
- indicator values for vascular plants from Tyler et al. (2021).

### 2.1 Spatial and temporal resolution and extent
The ANO export covers mainland Norway, 2019–2024. It holds `r cnt(nrow(plots))` surveys of wetland plots (NiN main types V1–V8) at `r cnt(n_distinct(plots$ano_punkt_id))` points in `r cnt(n_distinct(plots$ano_flate_id))` sites. Points are revisited on a five-year rotation, and the second rotation has only just begun. Three periods are reported: 2019–2021 and 2022–2024 (every survey in those years), and cycle 1 (2019–2024, first survey of each point, so no point is counted twice).

### 2.2 Sampling design
At each ANO site, vascular plants and their cover are recorded in a 1 m² plot at each of 18 systematically placed points (Tingstad et al., 2019). Only points that fall in wetland are used here, so the number of plots varies between sites.

### 2.3 Original units
Cover is recorded in per cent per 1 m² plot. The indicator values are ordinal: light 1–7, moisture 1–12, soil reaction 1–8 and nitrogen 1–9. The variable is the cover-weighted mean on the same scale.

### 2.4 Instructions for citing, using and accessing data

- **ANO**: open, [Miljødirektoratet dataset 2054](https://kartkatalog.miljodirektoratet.no/Dataset/Details/2054). Downloaded 2026-07-30 with `R/fetch_ano_data.R`.
- **B12**: open, [Artsdatabanken](https://artsdatabanken.no/Pages/281569/Generaliserte_artslistedatasett_til_artikkel_2). Downloaded 2026-08-03 with `R/fetch_b12_data.R`. On 2026-11-24 the site rejected downloads from scripts (HTTP 403), so the file must be downloaded in a web browser.
- **Tyler et al. (2021)**: supplementary material to the article. It must be downloaded by hand (2026-07-30) and is not redistributed here.

### 2.5 Additional comments about the dataset
Species without a match in Tyler et al. (2021) do not contribute to the CWM. `r cnt(sum(!is.na(plots$fac_Light)))` of the `r cnt(nrow(plots))` surveys get a value, see @tbl-types.

## 3. Indicator properties

### 3.1 Ecosystem Condition Typology Class (ECT)
Light and moisture are assigned to A1 (physical state), pH and nitrogen to A2 (chemical state). NINA uses the same classes for its light, moisture and nitrogen indicators.

### 3.2 Ecosystem condition characteristic
Abiotic factors, expressed through the species composition.

### 3.3 Collinearities with other indicators
The four indicators are derived from the same plant records and are therefore not independent of each other. Light may also covary with the woody encroachment indicators VAAT-GJEN-01 and VAAT-GJEN-02.

### 3.4 Impact factors
Drainage and other hydrological change (moisture), woody encroachment (light), nitrogen deposition and nutrient run-off (nitrogen), acidification and liming (pH), and climate change.

### 3.5 Spatial aggregation
The variable is scaled and truncated per plot. Regional and national values are means from an ordered beta regression on the plot values, with ANO site as a random effect. No area weighting is applied.

## 4. Reference condition and levels

### 4.1 Reference condition
The reference condition is largely intact ecosystems without large-scale human modification (Nybø & Evju, 2017). Here it is represented by the generalised species lists for each wetland type.

### 4.2 Reference levels
The reference levels are quantiles of the bootstrapped CWM distribution per NiN main type.

- **X~100~**: the median.
- **X~60~**: the 0.025 and 0.975 quantiles for the two-sided indicators; the 0.95 quantile for nitrogen.
- **X~0~**: the end of the indicator value scale.

The bootstrap uses NINA's function and settings: 1000 iterations per list, each keeping the dominant species and a random half of the others, with the cover classes varied.

```{r tbl-ref}
#| tbl-cap: "Reference levels per NiN main type (CWM quantiles)"
#| echo: false
ref |>
  mutate(indicator = factor(recode(indicator, Soil_reaction_pH = "pH"), fac_lv)) |>
  arrange(indicator, hovedtype) |>
  transmute(Indicator = indicator, `NiN type` = hovedtype, `Species lists` = n_lists,
            `0.025` = num(q025), `0.25` = num(q25), `Median (X100)` = num(median),
            `0.75` = num(q75), `0.95` = num(q95), `0.975` = num(q975)) |>
  kable()
```

#### 4.2.1 Spatial resolution and validity
The reference levels vary between wetland types, but not between regions. They are valid at plot level, which is where the scaling is done.

## 5. Uncertainties

### 5.1 General uncertainties

- **Reference per main type.** The references are set per NiN main type (V1, V2, V3), not per mapping unit as in NINA's original. Variation along the lime gradient within a main type is therefore part of the reference distribution.
- **Wetland types without a reference.** V6 has no reference, in NINA's original either. V4 and V8 have a reference in NINA's original, but not here, where the references are rebuilt from B12 only (@tbl-types).
- **Swamp forest.** ANO records V2 as one type, "myr- og sumpskogsmark". The V2 reference is built from 11 lists, all of forested peatland. A plot in swamp forest on mineral soil is therefore compared with forested peatland, and its pH and nitrogen may look like a deviation when they are not.
- **Regional bias.** NINA notes that the generalised species lists are biased towards southern and eastern Norway.
- **Observer and species uncertainty.** Uncertainty in the recorded cover and in the species' indicator values is not quantified.
- **No validation.** The indicators have not been validated against independent data.

```{r tbl-types}
#| tbl-cap: "Wetland plot surveys in ANO 2019–2024 and how many get a value, by NiN main type"
#| echo: false
type_names <- c(V1 = "Åpen jordvannsmyr", V2 = "Myr- og sumpskogsmark", V3 = "Nedbørsmyr",
                V4 = "Kaldkilde", V6 = "Våtsnøleie og snøleiekilde", V8 = "Strandsumpskogsmark")
plots |>
  group_by(nin) |>
  summarise(Surveys = n(), Scored = sum(!is.na(fac_Light)), .groups = "drop") |>
  transmute(`NiN type` = nin, Name = unname(type_names[nin]), Surveys, Scored) |>
  kable()
```

The `r sum(plots$nin %in% c("V1", "V2", "V3") & is.na(plots$fac_Light))` unscored surveys of types V1–V3 have no species records in the ANO export.

### 5.2 Reported uncertainties
The reported uncertainties are inferential and refer to the estimated mean. `sd` is the standard deviation, and the 95% interval the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles, of 1000 draws from the estimated coefficients of the regression. Uncertainty in the reference levels is not included.

## 6. References

Halvorsen, R., Skarpaas, O., Bryn, A., Bratli, H., Erikstad, L., Simensen, T., & Lieungh, E. (2020). Towards a systematics of ecodiversity: The EcoSyst framework. *Global Ecology and Biogeography, 29*(11), 1887–1906. <https://doi.org/10.1111/geb.13164> (the framework behind NiN and its generalised species lists)

Nybø, S., & Evju, M. (Eds.). (2017). *Fagsystem for fastsetting av god økologisk tilstand: Forslag fra et ekspertråd*. Ekspertrådet for økologisk tilstand.

Tingstad, L., Evju, M., Sickel, H., & Töpper, J. (2019). *Utvikling av nasjonal arealrepresentativ naturovervåking (ANO): Forslag til gjennomføring, protokoller og kostnadsvurderinger med utgangspunkt i erfaringer fra uttesting i Trøndelag* (NINA Rapport 1642). Norsk institutt for naturforskning.

Tyler, T., Herbertsson, L., Olofsson, J., & Olsson, P. A. (2021). Ecological indicator and traits values for Swedish vascular plants. *Ecological Indicators, 120*, 106923. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolind.2020.106923>

The method follows NINA's indicator documents [NO_FUNC_001–004](https://github.com/NINAnor/ecRxiv/tree/main/indicators/NO_FUNC_001-004), [NO_FULI_002](https://github.com/NINAnor/ecRxiv/tree/main/indicators/NO_FULI_002), [NO_FUMO_004](https://github.com/NINAnor/ecRxiv/tree/main/indicators/NO_FUMO_004), [NO_FUNI_002](https://github.com/NINAnor/ecRxiv/tree/main/indicators/NO_FUNI_002) and [NO_FUNI_004](https://github.com/NINAnor/ecRxiv/tree/main/indicators/NO_FUNI_004) on ecRxiv.

## 8. Spatial units

The basic spatial unit (BSU) is the 1 m² ANO plot. The indicator values should be interpreted for the ecosystem accounting areas (EAA): mainland Norway and five regions (Northern, Central, Western, Eastern and Southern Norway). The ecosystem asset (EA) is not delineated: wetland is identified by the NiN type recorded at the plot. The region polygons are taken from NINAnor/ecosystemCondition.

## 10. Results

### 10.1 The four indicators

```{r tbl-final}
#| tbl-cap: "Indicator values, ANO cycle 1 (2019–2024, first survey of each point). Mean [95% interval], n = plots"
#| echo: false
fac |>
  filter(period == main_period) |>
  mutate(factor = factor(factor, fac_lv), region = factor(region, reg_lv),
         cell = paste0(num(mean), " [", num(ci_low), "–", num(ci_high), "]")) |>
  arrange(region) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(region, n), names_from = factor, values_from = cell) |>
  select(Region = region, n, all_of(fac_lv)) |>
  kable()
```

Light is `r extremes("Light")`. Moisture is `r extremes("Moisture")`. pH is `r extremes("pH")`. Nitrogen is `r extremes("Nitrogen")`.

```{r fig-periods}
#| fig-cap: "Indicator values by region and period, with 95% intervals. The dashed line is the limit for good condition (0.6). Cycle 1 shares most of its surveys with the other two periods."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| echo: false
fac |>
  mutate(factor = factor(factor, fac_lv), region = factor(region, rev(reg_lv)),
         period = factor(period, c("2019to2021", "2022to2024", main_period),
                         c("2019–2021", "2022–2024", "Cycle 1 (2019–2024)"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(mean, region, colour = period, shape = period)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.6, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~factor) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#222222")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Indicator value", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r tbl-direction}
#| tbl-cap: "Direction of the deviations, Norway, cycle 1: number of plots on each side of the reference median, and the mean value of those plots. Nitrogen is one-sided, so only plots with enrichment are counted."
#| echo: false
dash <- function(x, f) ifelse(is.na(x), "–", f(x))
nat |>
  mutate(factor = factor(factor, fac_lv)) |>
  arrange(factor) |>
  transmute(Indicator = factor,
            `Plots below` = dash(n_lower, cnt), `Mean below` = dash(mean_lower, num),
            `Plots above` = dash(n_upper, cnt), `Mean above` = dash(mean_upper, num)) |>
  kable(align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r fig-map}
#| fig-cap: "Indicator values per region, ANO cycle 1 (2019–2024)"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
#| echo: false
ids <- c(Light = "VAAT-FULI-01", Moisture = "VAAT-FUMO-01", pH = "VAAT-FUPH-01", Nitrogen = "VAAT-FUNI-01")
maps <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ids), function(f) {
  m <- readRDS(file.path("..", "outputs", "deliverables",
                         paste0(ids[[f]], "_cycle1_2019to2024_indicatorMap_region.rds")))
  m <- st_simplify(m, dTolerance = 1000)
  m$factor <- f
  m[, c("area", "i_2024", "factor")]
}))
st_agr(maps) <- "constant"
maps$factor <- factor(maps$factor, fac_lv)
ggplot(maps) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = i_2024), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf_label(aes(label = num(i_2024)), fill = "white", size = 2.4, label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines")) +
  facet_wrap(~factor, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0.6, 1), name = "Indicator\nvalue") +
  theme_void() + theme(plot.margin = margin(2, 12, 2, 2))
```

### 10.2 Distribution of plot values

```{r fig-dist}
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of scaled plot values, all surveys 2019–2024. The dashed line is 0.6."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| echo: false
plots |>
  select(all_of(paste0("fac_", fac_lv))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "factor", names_prefix = "fac_") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(factor = factor(factor, fac_lv)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0, fill = "#0072B2", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.6, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~factor, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Scaled plot value", y = "Plots") +
  theme_bw()
```

### 10.3 Combined index (not delivered)

The pipeline also calculates the combined index of NINA's NO_FUNC indicators. It is not part of the delivery, and its files are in `outputs/supplementary/`. It takes the lowest of the eight scaled sides per plot, uses the 0.25 and 0.75 quantiles as limits (as in NINA's code for NO_FUNC_001–004; the text of that document states 0.025 and 0.975), and is aggregated as a median. Its values are not comparable with the four indicators above.

```{r tbl-index}
#| tbl-cap: "Combined index VAAT-FUNC-01: median [95% bootstrap interval], n = plots"
#| echo: false
idx |>
  mutate(region = factor(region, reg_lv),
         cell = paste0(num(median), " [", num(boot_low), "–", num(boot_high), "], n = ", cnt(n)),
         period = recode(period, "2019to2021" = "2019–2021", "2022to2024" = "2022–2024",
                         "cycle1_2019to2024" = "Cycle 1 (2019–2024)")) |>
  arrange(region) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = region, names_from = period, values_from = cell) |>
  rename(Region = region) |>
  kable()
```
